label: a8-11-def-locally-compact-space
tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_NONFATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/def-locally-compact-space.md lines 70–71, metric characterization block
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “then $K$ contains the open set $B(x,r)$, which contains $x$, so $K$ is a neighbourhood of $x$ and is compact.”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: items/def-metric-ball.md says, “The names "open ball" and "closed ball" are justified, not merely suggestive.” and “the words are used here only as names for the three sets displayed above.” The omitted items/thm-metric-open-set-algebra.md states, “Balls are open. $B(x,r)$ is open”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The judge correctly identifies an omitted justification: the cited ball definition does not establish openness and points elsewhere for it. This is nonfatal under the binding 30-second rule. Given y in B(x,r), take s equal to r minus d(x,y). Then s is positive, and the triangle inequality gives B(y,s) contained in B(x,r). This immediately proves openness from the metric axioms and the definition of the metric topology. The same argument closes the later use of open balls in the Euclidean witness. The omission is a short local derivation or citation gap, not a false claim or missing hypothesis.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
